history.summary: A CDL-built 1,098 sqft 3BR in Pasir Ris, 480m from Pasir Ris MRT/interchange, asking $1,685 PSF — marginally below the $1,696 median, with a healthy 6.3% URA resale CAGR over 234 transactions. The fundamentals are sound and well-priced, but the cluster of ~3,000 CDL units in Pasir Ris Grove (Coco Palms, plus siblings) and further upcoming supply create persistent rental and resale competition that holds this to a solid Buy rather than Strong.
history.rating_rationale: Good value-for-quality: large 944-unit CDL development gives strong liquidity, $1.85M quantum sits in the deep buyer band, $1,685 PSF is just under the $1,696 median (no overpay), and a 6.3% URA resale-only CAGR over a deep 234 transactions evidences real demand. 480m to Pasir Ris MRT plus the future RTS/interchange improvements support D18. Capped at Buy by the well-documented Pasir Ris Grove supply overhang — 3,000+ CDL units clustered together plus additional plots slated nearer the MRT — which intensifies rental competition and could cap resale pricing power; score 711 is good but off-frontier.
red_flags: Pasir Ris Grove supply overhang — ~3,000 clustered CDL units plus further plots slated nearer the MRT, pressuring rents and resale
OCR location with no freehold/scarcity premium — relies on continued OCR demand
catalysts: 6.3% URA resale CAGR over a deep 234 txns — well-evidenced demand

480m to Pasir Ris MRT/interchange; Pasir Ris town rejuvenation and future connectivity
Large 944-unit CDL development — strong liquidity and amenities

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Mixed. Family-friendly large 3BR but the Pasir Ris Grove cluster means heavy direct rental competition; achievable rents and occupancy are pressured versus a standalone development. Yield ~3%.

history.summary: The cleanest name of the cohort: a cheap small unit in a proven-outperforming OCR mega-condo with deep, trustworthy transaction data and a dated MRT catalyst. Value, liquidity and region all align.
history.rating_rationale: Asking $1,391 psf for a 624 sqft unit sits well below the project's recent small-unit prints — a 463 sqft unit hit $1,836 psf (Jun 2025) and a 743 sqft unit went for $1,696 psf (Jan 2026), with a 12-month project avg of ~$1,684 psf. So the -13.4% age-adj and -17.7% cohort premiums are backed by real, recent, same-size comparables. Crucially the data is deep — 234 appreciation txns and 18 cohort txns — so this is not a thin-data quirk; confidence is high. D18 is OCR, the strongest forward region under v3.4 priors (realized fwd ~+4.0%), and Coco Palms has independently been documented as a top-performing 99LH condo 2014-2025. The +6.3% trailing CAGR is treated as story not guarantee, but here it is corroborated by a confirmed catalyst.
red_flags: 99-year leasehold from 2008 (~82 years left) — fine now but the clock matters on a 5-7yr hold-and-exit
944-unit mega-development means heavy internal supply competition on both resale and rental at any given time
Asking $1,391 psf is at/near the bottom of the recent range — verify the specific unit's facing/floor isn't the reason for the discount
catalysts: Cross Island Line Pasir Ris interchange (CR5, Phase 1 ~2030) plus CRL-Punggol Extension (~2032), both confirmed and under/approaching construction
Verified ~17% discount to recent same-size transactions on deep liquidity
OCR region with the strongest realized forward appreciation in the v3.4 backtest
Documented top-quartile historical ROI vs 99LH peers; resort-style amenities support rental demand
